overview: These are about as bare-bones as wireless modules get: two separate tiny boards (one transmitter, one receiver), each with no microcontroller, no protocol, no addressing, and no error checking — the transmitter just broadcasts whatever digital signal it's given as raw ASK/OOK radio pulses, and the receiver spits out whatever it picks up, noise included. That means unlike an HC-12 or NRF24L01, all the packetization and error-detection work has to happen in software (commonly via a library like RC-Switch), but the tradeoff is an extremely cheap way to send simple on/off style commands — exactly like the remote for a garage door or wireless doorbell, which is precisely what these modules are often salvaged from or designed to mimic.
simpleSummary: A very basic pair of radio modules for sending simple signals wirelessly, with no smarts built in.

specifications.modulation: ASK/OOK (on-off keying) — no built-in packetization or error correction
specifications.range: ~50-100m open air with a proper antenna, much less with a short/no antenna
specifications.dataRate: Low — a few kbps at most, and unreliable without a tolerant encoding scheme

pinMap.name: TX DATA
pinMap.function: Transmitter's digital input — whatever HIGH/LOW pattern is applied here is broadcast as radio pulses.

pinMap.name: TX ANT
pinMap.function: Antenna connection — typically just a length of wire cut to a specific length for the 433MHz wavelength.
pinMap.gotcha: Range without a properly-sized antenna wire can drop to just a few centimeters — this is the most common 'why doesn't this work' issue with these modules.

pinMap.name: RX DATA
pinMap.function: Receiver's digital output — outputs whatever it picks up, including noise when no signal is present.
pinMap.gotcha: With no transmitter active, this pin doesn't sit cleanly LOW — it outputs random noise, so software must use a proper decoding scheme (like RC-Switch) rather than treating raw transitions as valid data.

useCases.title: Simple wireless remote control
useCases.scenario: Send basic on/off commands to a remote relay (e.g. wireless light switch) using the RC-Switch library.

useCases.title: Garage door / gate remote clone
useCases.scenario: Capture and replay a fixed-code remote's signal (for compatible legacy systems only).

oftenConfusedWith: HC-12 (has its own onboard protocol handling, far more reliable)
oftenUpgradedTo: HC-12 or NRF24L01 for reliable, addressable communication instead of raw broadcast
